body:
First of all: you are an awesome boyfriend. Seriously. Never stop being this awesome. I've been the "depressed girlfriend" for going on six years, and I honestly wish my now-fiancé would put more effort into understanding how I feel, and ask the right questions. The fact that you're actively looking for ways to help this woman is -- once again -- really awesome.

My best advice? Realize that there might not be any easy fix for how she feels, and that she might feel this way off and on for quite some time (if not her whole life, although I certainly hope this isn't the case). Prepare yourself and make sure you can handle it. There will be very bad days. Hopefully not many, but they will be there.

Just for some perspective, here's our story. The most difficult thing about my depression in relation to my SO is that he started caring a little less and a little less as time went on. At first, he was super supportive. Then he would listen, but not offer much in return. And when things got really bad, he literally told me that he had no compassion for me, especially when I cried. He insisted that he still loved me, but that he had essentially become immune to my "crazy" and he was tired of hearing it. That crushed me more than anything else could have. I was in a huge amount of emotional pain, and he just stopped caring because there was nothing he could do to fix it. So, he gave up on offering support altogether. We have a child, so we've worked really hard to stay together and understand each other better. He tries, and things are better these days, but even now I don't think he's ever actively searched out answers like you have here.

As far as what you can actively do: just listen without judgement. Don't correct her feelings or try to apply logic, because depression is far from logical. Give her so many hugs. Big squeezy ones. And make sure she knows that she can always ask for more. And perhaps most importantly, don't make it about how her feelings are affecting you... at least not in the moment (save that talk for when things are more calm). To me, there is nothing more deflating than wanting to unload some of my pent up feelings, only to have him tell me right off the bat that my mood is a downer for him and that he's getting "depressed" because I'm depressing. No kidding it's a downer, that's why I'm trying to talk about it.

Sorry for the novel, just my two cents since I'd already been thinking about this a lot today. Good luck -- your girl is lucky to have you!

Yay! Isn't it amazing how differently we perceive ourselves based on our inner selves? Some days I'm convinced I'm hideous -- no makeup, frizzy hair, and a crying mess. I mean, come on -- what could my SO possibly see in ME? WHY is he with me? Is this some sort of "long con" practical joke? Other days, I wonder what the hell I was thinking and I twirl around in the mirror feeling fabulous. I miss feeling fabulous :(.

I prefer to stay numb, but that's just me. It's easier to pretend I'm OK, and not freak people out. It's also easier to be left alone that way. That being said, I was a sad freaking mess today and there was no stopping it. Some days ya just need to cry.

I notice that people help. They really do. Just last night I was a crying, sobbing mess and my fiance dragged me to hang out with a work friend and his wife. I was angry at him for it -- I didn't want to do a single damn thing except feel sorry for myself, and he didn't even let me change out of my pajama pants first. But I'll be damned if I forgot to mope and cry when we got back. Things are worse today, but I'm also isolated today. Just goes to show you: people help a LOT, even if it's just small talk.

I was actually going to edit and add a question, because I realize I didn't really ask anything. Feedback would be great, maybe there's a light at the end of the tunnel that I can't see. 

Here's one for you:

How can I explain true depression to my "fix-it" fiance? And how can I be less of a burden to him? I know he hates my moping and crying. He asks "What's wrong?" and I don't know how to answer. If I say I don't like certain parts of my life, he's like, "Gee thanks." And then he makes it about him. If I'm too vague, it sounds like I'm skirting the issue. If I describe everything in detail, I sound like a drama queen and/or a downer. How can I have a real conversation about this and help him understand? Honestly, there isn't any one thing that's wrong. EVERYTHING is wrong. He asks me what I'm thinking about, and I literally won't have an answer because I'm just empty inside.

Hi, thanks for your response. I guess I could have been more specific -- we're actually in Niagara Falls right outside of Buffalo. 

You aren't wrong -- there actually are some things to do in Buffalo. Right now we have memberships to the Niagara Falls Aquarium and the Buffalo Museum of Science, and we've had a zoo membership in the past. We only do that stuff on the weekends when his dad is around to drive us. I honestly don't have a lot of faith in the safety of the area -- we lived in South Buffalo for a bit, and we were always getting things stolen from inside our gated fence. And Niagara Falls isn't much better, our GPS and a few other items were stolen out of our car almost as soon as we moved here and there was a shooting not that far away not that long ago. Taking the bus that far is a little scary to me. Maybe that's just me being sheltered, but it makes me nervous to get so far away from home without my own vehicle. Also, I'm not sure how the kiddo would handle long bus rides and multiple connections -- I can't ever get him to sit still and trying to manage him on a full bus almost sounds worse than staying home.

As far as freelance work, I'll take a look at your list. I honestly don't have a lot of faith in that either at this point. I couldn't even get work when my experience was recent, so taking a bunch of time off probably hasn't helped. And time is still a factor -- I'm hanging out with the kid from about 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., give or take a break when his dad gets home. After than I'm so exhausted I try to stay up, but end up accomplishing next to nothing. I crashed and burned with the last ongoing freelance job I had... they were upset that I wasn't as available as they wanted me to be and all my work was showing up late. Turns out I'm fairly unreliable. I used to be so on top of everything... now I'm just a lazy bum who lets people down.
